stories.headline: Yankees waiting to decide on Aaron Judge's availability for ALDS
stories.summary: The Yankees have not decided if Aaron Judge will be on their roster for the ALDS vs. the Rays as he continues to work his way back from a right calf strain.
stories.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- The Yankees have not decided if Aaron Judge will be on their roster for the American League Division Series against the Rays as he continues to work his way back from a right calf strain, manager Aaron Boone said Friday.

The Yankees have until Saturday morning to submit their roster. Game 1 is scheduled for Saturday at 6:30 p.m. ET.

"We'll see," Boone said.

Judge has not played since straining his calf -- specifically his soleus muscle -- Sept. 16. The Yankees considered including him on their wild-card series roster but proceeded without him and still throttled the Red Sox, outscoring their rivals 18-2 in the two-game sweep at Yankee Stadium.

In his push to convince the team's brass he is ready, Judge faced live pitching at Yankee Stadium on Thursday and worked out at the organization's minor league complex in Tampa early Friday before joining the team for its afternoon workout at Tropicana Field. It was the third time this week the three-time MVP hit against live pitching. He took BP at Tropicana Field on Friday.

While Judge also began running this week, Boone said he was not sure if Judge has run the bases yet. He indicated that running the bases is not a prerequisite for having Judge on the roster.

"Sometimes running the bases, they replicate things in other ways," Boone said. "The trainers will obviously play a big part in this. As the day unfolds, we'll see where we're at and what it potentially looks like for the series."

Boone said Tropicana Field's turf surface -- less than ideal for a 6-foot-7, 280-pound athlete coming off a calf injury -- will factor into the team's decision-making "a little bit" before hinting at the possibility of carrying Judge on the roster but him being limited early in the series.

"It's just as far as him and the field, potentially," Boone said. "But we're looking at the days, and so it's more, 'Is he going to be available at some point in this series, potentially, as a player?' That's what we're kind of weighing and then seeing where he's at now these last few days having taken live BP."

With Ben Rice entrenched at designated hitter and Paul Goldschmidt and Luis Garcia platooning at first base, Judge would ideally return to play right field. Judge has insisted that's his goal. If he's not cleared for that for the first two games, he could be used as a pinch hitter off the bench then and start playing in the field when the series goes to New York for Game 3 on Wednesday.

"I was thinking that Aaron Judge was going to be there a week ago just so I'm not devastated when he's on," Rays manager Kevin Cash said Friday. "I expect him playing right field, hitting third."

Giancarlo Stanton, who has not played in a game since sustaining a calf strain in April, was on the Yankees' wild-card series roster in that pinch-hitter role but didn't get an at-bat in either game. On Friday, Stanton, MLB's active home run leader, said he is "ready to go" for whatever is asked.

Ryan Weathers, another roster uncertainty, said he tossed a bullpen Wednesday after facing hitters Monday. He has not pitched in a game since Aug. 22, when he exited a start with a forearm flexor strain. If he is put on the roster, he would return as a one-inning reliever and likely wouldn't be cleared to pitch on consecutive days. "I don't know if there's been final decisions," Weathers said. "Obviously, I feel super healthy enough to be on it."

Boone said the team is considering whether to include 10, 11 or 12 pitchers on the roster after carrying 10 pitchers and 16 position players in the wild-card round. One pitcher definitely on the roster is Gerrit Cole, who will take the mound for New York in Game 1 for his first postseason start since Game 5 of the 2024 World Series.

Cole, 36, will take the mound on nine days' rest. His 22nd and final regular-season start after returning from Tommy John surgery was at Yankee Stadium, also against the Rays. The right-hander threw a season-high 105 pitches over 5⅓ innings, allowing two runs on three hits with eight strikeouts and three walks.

"It's incredibly special," Cole said. "And considering coming back from surgery, I mean, there's not much more I could ask for."

Boone said the club considered choosing left-hander Carlos Rodón, who was on the wild-card series roster as a reliever but didn't pitch, to start Game 1. Instead, Boone said Rodón will "probably" start Game 3 or 4, though he did not shut down the possibility of Rodón coming out of the bullpen in one of the first two games against a team that ranked 26th in the majors in wRC+ against lefties.

Cam Schlittler, coming off a dominant performance in Game 1 against Boston, is expected to start Game 2 on Monday. Rodón and fellow left-hander Max Fried, in some order, would take the ball the next two games, with Game 4 only as necessary in the best-of-five series.

"We've got four starters," Boone said. "You're going to see them. How we line them up is a different conversation."

stories.headline: 49ers WR Mike Evans a game-time decision with rib injury
stories.summary: Niners wide receiver Mike Evans is questionable for Sunday, but said he's going to give "my best" to play against the Broncos as he deals with a rib injury.
stories.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans is questionable for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos and will be a game-time decision, according to coach Kyle Shanahan.

But Evans, who was a limited participant in Friday's practice after missing Wednesday and Thursday, said he is going to give "my best" to play against the Broncos despite his painful rib injury.

"It's my job," Evans said. "I take pride in trying to suit up every chance I get. If the injury isn't unbearable and you can't play through it, then I won't play. But if there's something I can play through, I'm going to be there for my team as best I can."

On Friday, Evans spoke to the media for the first time since suffering the injury in the first half of last week's win against the Arizona Cardinals. He said he wasn't sure when, exactly, the injury happened but on the play where he left the game, he was running a route, turned and then it "felt like somebody stabbed me in my chest."

Evans went to the ground and then slowly made his way to the sideline before he went to the locker room on a cart. Asked if he thought the injury happened earlier, Evans said he couldn't pinpoint anything other than a big hit from Cardinals safety Budda Baker, but he said he felt that in his head more than his chest or rib area.

While Evans' status will loom until closer to game time, he sounded like someone pushing to play. He said he doesn't plan to use a flak jacket because it "looks kind of weak" and it's more for quarterbacks. But Evans said a padding option will be important and he's hoping to use a compression shirt that has some built into it.

Evans said he has previously played through a rib injury. His game log shows that while he was a member of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, he had a rib injury in November 2022. He was limited in practice before playing against the Seattle Seahawks and posting five catches for 54 yards in a 21-16 win.

According to Evans, the key to playing through such an injury is getting adequate padding surrounding the rib while also making sure to take extra time to warm your body up before playing.

"It was brutal to play through," Evans said. "But it's something that I can do."

Shanahan, who recently dealt with three broken ribs from a car accident in July, also offered some hope that Evans will play against Denver.

"I would be out without a doubt," Shanahan said, laughing. "But he's definitely a lot tougher than me. So, hopefully we've got a shot."

Elsewhere on the injury report, the Niners ruled out defensive end Nick Bosa (calf), defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. (ankle) and defensive lineman Mykel Williams (knee).

Like Evans, linebacker Dre Greenlaw (quad) and defensive lineman Keion White (hamstring) are questionable after missing practice Wednesday and Thursday and then working on a limited basis Friday.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Jadon Sancho willing to wait for January move
stories.summary: Jadon Sancho is happy to wait to sign for a club. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Free agent Jadon Sancho is happy to wait to sign for a club, while Tomás Araújo is subject to interest from Manchester United and Chelsea.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Jadon Sancho is willing to hold out until January as a free agent before making a decision, if the right offer doesn't arrive before then, reports TEAMtalk. The former Manchester United and Borussia Dortmund winger is a free agent, following his exit from Old Trafford at the end of his contract in the summer. The 26-year-old has been linked with a whole host of clubs since, but is yet to make a decision on his future, with nothing advanced on his next club.

- Manchester United and Chelsea are monitoring a deal for Benfica defender Tomás Araújo, according to TEAMTalk. The 24-year-old is claimed to be on the radar of several Premier League clubs, but it's United and Chelsea who are most keen. Araujo, who can play center back and right-back, recently signed a contract extension until 2031, making an exit in January unlikely. However, with a release clause valued at £68 million, clubs could pursue a switch anyway

- Juventus are preparing a huge rebuild over the next year, with Tuttosport naming a whole host of potential transfer targets for the Italian club. In the goalkeeping ranks, Alisson Becker is claimed to be a player of interest, as he could leave Liverpool at the end of the season as a free agent. In defence, Oumar Solet of Udinese is viewed as an option, while RB Leipzig ace David Raum and Crystal Palace star Tyrick Mitchell are also on the Bianconeri's radar. Napoli stalwart Stanislav Lobotka, Manchester City midfielder Mateo Kovacic, and Real Madrid playmaker Brahim Díaz are touted as options for the central ranks. Meanwhile, Crystal Palace forward Jean-Philippe Mateta could be a striker arrival.

- João Félix is keen on making a return to Barcelona next year, when the Portuguese international's contract with Al Nassr is set to expire. That's according to Sport, which reports that the 27-year-old has his sights set on a return to the Champions League after a recent resurgence in his career in the Saudi Pro League. Felix previously spent a year on loan with Barcelona from Atletico Madrid, where he made 44 appearances with 10 goals and six assists. Now back in form, and eyeing a possible free transfer, a return to the Nou Camp is on his mind, though the report claims that he is not viewed as a priority target.

- Juventus have declared that Kenan Yildiz and Kerim Alajbegovic are "untouchable" in future transfer markets, with the club keen to build around the pair, reports La Gazzetta. Yildiz, 21, has previously attracted interest from Arsenal and Real Madrid, having shown plenty of potential. The forward ended up staying with Juventus over the summer, though a recent injury issue means he will be out until December. As for Alajbegovic, the Bianconeri managed to beat plenty of competition to his signature from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer transfer window. With the 19-year-old forward featuring for the club since, and reports of potential interest from the likes of Chelsea in the future, Juventus have set a clear stance of no exit for now.

Other rumors
- Inter Milan remain keen on a future move for Leeds United defender Tarik Muharemovic, after missing out on the 23-year-old in the summer. Barcelona are also among the clubs keeping track of the Bosnia and Herzegovina international. (TeamTalk)

- Arsenal continue to track a move for Junior Kroupi, with PSG also following proceedings for the Bournemouth forward, who is ramping up his recovery from an injury that has prevented him from playing this season. (Ekrem Konur)

- Manchester United are set to open talks with Luke Shaw over an extension to his contract, with the left back entering the final 12 months of his deal. (Ekrem Konur)

- Serie A side Bologna are set to sign former Manchester United and Inter Milan defender Matteo Darmian as a free agent on a one-year deal, following an injury to Emil Holm. (Fabrizio Romano)

- Bologna are also planning to extend the contract of Federico Bernardeschi, with the 32-year-old forward entering the last year of his two-year deal. (Nicolo Schira)

- Former Manchester City winger Riyad Mahrez is closing in on a move to Qatar-based team Al Shamal as a free agent, after the 35-year-old left Saudi Pro League side Al Ahli in the summer. (Nicolo Schira)

- Arsenal, Manchester United, and Chelsea are all set to battle it out for Como defender Jacobo Ramon, with the 21-year-old centre-back catching the eye under Cesc Fabregas. (Caught Offside)

- Club Tijuana and Mexico playmaker Gilberto Mora, 17, would prefer a transfer move to La Liga over the Premier League in the coming months. Liverpool, Barcelona, and Real Madrid have all shown interest. (Football Insider)

stories.headline: WNBA championship and Finals MVP odds: Aces backs as favorites after ousting Fever
stories.summary: The Las Vegas Aces are back to being the favorites for the WNBA title after advancing past the Indiana Fever.
stories.body:
The Las Vegas Aces are back to being the favorites for the WNBA title after defeating the Indiana Fever in a hard-fought first-round series, showing +160 odds at DraftKings. Bookmakers across the sportsbook marketplace are likely breathing a sigh of relief with the Fever eliminated, as Caitlin Clark's crew were a popular futures play all season and, thus, a huge liability.

The Atlanta Dream are second on the championship odds board at +240, followed by the Golden State Valkyries at +390. The New York Liberty were briefly the title favorites after taking down the previously favored Minnesota Lynx in two games, but they have fallen to fourth on the odds board at +450 with other teams advancing. The Dallas Wings round out the board at a distant 70-1.

stories.headline: Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Charles Leclerc tops second practice, Mercedes off the pace
stories.summary: Charles Leclerc topped the timesheets in second practice at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, with the session staying dry despite the threat of rain.
stories.body:
Charles Leclerc topped the timesheets in second practice at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, with the session staying dry despite the threat of rain.

The Ferrari driver set the time halfway through the session on the soft compound tyre and crossed the line 0.099 seconds ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar.

McLaren's Lando Norris was third-fastest, with Max Verstappen behind. The Dutchamn, who was fastest in first practice, spent the session doing long runs on the medium tyre, while the majority of the grid were on the soft tyres.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton rounded out the top five and was three-tenths off his teammate Leclerc's pace.

McLaren made some adjustments to Norris' rear wing to get the 'Macarena' style rear wing that Oscar Piastri was using in first practice on Friday.

Piastri ended the second session in sixth, while Mercedes duo George Russell and title leader Kimi Antonelli were off the pace and finished down in seventh and eighth respectively. Both drivers were on soft tyres but had to abort their flying laps.

- Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Max Verstappen leads first practice from George Russell

- Lewis Hamilton hits out at Ferrari hierarchy in Fred Vasseur defence: 'Point fingers somewhere else'

Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto complained on the team radio that Hamilton got in his way on track, while the seven-time champion reported that "he can't see through" his right mirror. Hamilton was sent to the stewards and has received a warning, while Ferrari were fined €10,000 (£8,503).

Bortoleto also brought out the Virtual Safety Car in the closing stages of the session.

Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson was ninth and Alpine's Pierre Gasly rounded out the top 10.

stories.headline: MMA 30 under 30: Champions Joshua Van and Usman Nurmagomedov lead
stories.summary: The future is now! Joshua Van, Usman Nurmagomedov and more championship-caliber fighters top 30 under 30 list.
stories.body:
ESPN's yearly list of the top 30 fighters under age 30 can be characterized as a look into the future. These are the young fighters who presumably will take over once the sport's top veterans move on.

But this year's ranking is not merely forward thinking.

Consider that the top two fighters -- Joshua Van in the UFC and Usman Nurmagomedov in the PFL -- aren't rising prospects. They are defending champions. No. 3 Ilia Topuria is a former UFC champion. And Natalia Silva, who sits at No. 9, will go for the vacant women's flyweight title this weekend at UFC 332. In MMA, it seems, "the future is now" is not simply a catchy slogan.

There also are up-and-comers in these rankings, as there are every year, and many who have appeared before are now in different positions, as a year's worth of fight results dictates.

Our panel -- Brett Okamoto, Dre Waters, Jeff Wagenheim, Andrew Davis, James Regan, Sam Bruce, James Dielhenn, Marcus Vanderberg and Alecia Hamm -- selected fighters based on their achievements this year and their potential. Okamoto, Waters and Wagenheim provide breakdowns of the top 30 under 30.

1. Joshua Van

UFC men's flyweight champion

Age: 24

2025 rank: 3

It takes a remarkable athlete to lead this type of list -- but to lead it at 24 years old is just absurd. Van is arguably the purest talent the sport has seen in years. No one could have predicted at the start of 2025, when his ascension truly took off, that he would end the year as ESPN's best breakout fighter. He is undeniably the best active flyweight on the planet and has the personality and charisma to match. Sean O'Malley recently proclaimed on his YouTube channel that Van will go down as the "greatest flyweight of all time." After Van's second win over former longtime champion Alexandre Pantoja at UFC 331, who wants to disagree? -- Okamoto

2. Usman Nurmagomedov

PFL lightweight champion

Age: 28

2025 rank: 7

It's unusual for a fighter outside the UFC to establish himself as the best in his weight class, but that's exactly what Nurmagomedov has done with his perfect 21-0 record. It's not unreasonable to suggest Nurmagomedov would be favored against any other 155-pound fighter in the world, including top-ranked UFC lightweights Justin Gaethje, Arman Tsarukyan and Ilia Topuria. Nurmagomedov is currently a free agent, and his next move is one of the biggest questions in MMA this year. -- Okamoto

3. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Age: 29

2025 rank: 1

Topuria entered the year as the UFC lightweight champion, ESPN's top-ranked fighter under 30 and on the short list of the best pound-for-pound fighters in the world. He got his first chance to defend the belt in a main event at the White House on June 14, but the challenger, Gaethje, handed him the first loss of his professional career, retiring him on the stool after four rounds. Despite the loss, Topuria remains one of MMA's best young fighters. -- Waters

4. Michael Morales

UFC welterweight

Age: 27

2025 rank: 5

Fans love a good knockout, and Morales has handed out KOs regularly on his way to the welterweight title picture. Three consecutive first-round finishes have all the momentum on Morales's side, but he hasn't fought yet this year. He's on champion Islam Makhachev's radar as a future welterweight challenger, but he'll likely need one more win against a top contender to get his first title shot. -- Okamoto

5. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL women's flyweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: 2

One of the most destructive figures in women's MMA, Ditcheva is uniquely violent, boasting a 73% knockout rate in the PFL. The question isn't whether she can be a star, it's how big her star can become. With Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions acquiring the PFL going into 2027, we will find out what the ceiling is for Ditcheva's exposure. She is exactly the kind of marketable athlete MVP will get behind. -- Okamoto

6. Song Yadong

UFC men's bantamweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: 28

Song put two years of little activity behind him by fighting three times in the first eight months of 2026. He lost a tight decision to Sean O'Malley in January, but he bounced back in May against another champion, choking out Deiveson Figueiredo. But what elevated Song most on this list -- he was way down at No. 28 last year -- was his knockout of Umar Nurmagomedov in August. That stunning result boosted Song's stock as a men's bantamweight contender. Next up should be another ranked opponent, giving him an opportunity to build off of his recent success. -- Wagenheim

7. Josh Hokit

UFC heavyweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

Hokit's antics on the microphone may not have endeared him to UFC CEO Dana White, who said at UFC 331 that he doesn't like anything Hokit says. But the heavyweight's performance in his second year in the Octagon has skyrocketed him to the top of the division. "I say it all the time: I don't have to like you for you to thrive here and you to do well and be successful," White said of Hokit's ascension. With just four UFC fights under his belt -- three this year -- Hokit is set to challenge Ciryl Gane for the heavyweight championship in the main event at UFC 334 in November. Hokit, who earned a contract on Season 9 of "Dana White's Contender Series" just 13 months ago, already has beaten heavyweight stalwarts Curtis Blaydes and Derrick Lewis in two of the more entertaining fights of the year. Ending 2026 with a UFC championship would be an impressive cap to his year. -- Waters

8. Ian Machado Garry

UFC welterweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: 6

Love him or hate him, Machado Garry might be the best UFC welterweight not named Islam Makhachev. He took the pound-for-pound king five competitive rounds in August and is still in great position to accept some of the biggest fights available as he works his way back toward a second title shot. Machado Garry has said he believes that a loss to Makhachev will only make him better, and there are plenty of reasons to believe the 28-year-old's best is still in front of him. -- Okamoto

9. Natalia Silva

UFC women's flyweight

Age: 29

2025 rank: 9

Silva might be a UFC champion by the end of the weekend. By winning 14 fights in a row, the past eight in the Octagon, she has been looking more and more like championship material. Her three most recent wins came against former titleholders Jessica Andrade, Alexa Grasso and Rose Namajunas. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva is poised to take over if she handles Wang Cong at UFC 332. Women's flyweight is a highly competitive division, with several pound-for-pound elites. It could be Silva's domain until someone figures out how to contend with her slick movement. -- Wagenheim

10. Quillan Salkilld

UFC lightweight

Age: 26

2025 rank: 23

Somehow, even in a division full of potential superstars, Australia's Salkilld has managed to stand out -- and not just because he has a great mustache. Salkilld's got a look and presence on social media that plays well with the UFC's fanbase, and he has substance to back up the flash. He is on a streak of five consecutive first-round finishes, including in his most recent win, in which he beat submission artist Mateusz Gamrot at his own game with a first-round rear-naked choke. Salkilld has that "it" factor, and if he keeps winning, he will collide with some of the sport's biggest names. -- Okamoto

11. Jean Silva

UFC featherweight

Age: 29

Last year's rank: 15

Silva was denied a higher-profile opportunity when his Noche UFC opponent, popular and flashy Yair Rodriguez, withdrew from last month's fight because of injury. Silva did not suffer a letdown against late replacement Jose Miguel Delgado, taking care of business by doing what he usually does: making the fight his showcase. The win was Silva's second in a row after a September 2025 knockout loss ended a 13-fight winning streak. Silva is building himself toward featherweight contention with an aggressive fighting style that is a dream for fans and a nightmare for opponents. -- Wagenheim

12. Tatsuro Taira

UFC men's flyweight

Age: 26

Last year's rank: 22

Taira won eight of his first nine UFC fights, a run of success capped by a knockout of former two-time men's flyweight champion Brandon Moreno in December. But it was a loss that drew more attention to him -- positive attention. Taira ended up being knocked out by current champion Joshua Van in a title fight in May, but it was a back-and-forth fight that lasted into the fifth round. Taira put the champ in trouble with eight takedowns and over 10 minutes of control time. It was fight of the night, keeping the Japanese fighter in the contender conversation. -- Wagenheim

13. Navajo Stirling

UFC light heavyweight

Age: 28

Last year's rank: NR

Entering 2026, all three of Stirling's UFC wins had come by unanimous decision, but that stretch seems like an anomaly now. Stirling earned a UFC contract via a second-round knockout on "Dana White's Contender Series" in 2024 and had knocked out three of his four professional opponents before that. He officially refound his finishing ways this year, winning each of his three fights by knockout, including a first-round TKO over former light heavyweight champion Jan Blachowicz in August. Stirling may not have opened the year nearing his first title shot, but if he can take down another former champion in JiYí Procházka on Nov. 21, he'll end the year near the top of the light heavyweight contenders short list. -- Waters

14. Thad Jean

PFL welterweight champion

Age: 28

Last year's rank: NR

The PFL has asked several figures to be the "face of the company" over the years with mixed results. Recently much of that promotional expectation has been heaped on Jean, the 28-year-old who won the 2025 welterweight tournament. Jean has legitimate skills and highlight-reel potential. He's styled on the opponents he should have, and has proven his world-class merit with hard-fought wins over tougher opponents such as Logan Storley and Jason Jackson. -- Okamoto

15. Gabriel Bonfim

UFC welterweight

Age: 29

Last year's rank: 21

Bonfim is another fighter on this list who could be nearing a title shot. He only has competed once this year, but was dominant in a five-round unanimous decision win over former welterweight champion Belal Muhammad. All three judges scored the fight 50-45 for Bonfirm, who claimed the No. 7 spot in ESPN's divisional rankings as a result. Bonfim's biggest hurdle going forward will be the rise in competition in a stacked 170-pound division. His next test will come against No. 6-ranked Sean Brady on Nov. 7. -- Waters

16. Salahdine Parnasse

UFC lightweight

Age: 28

Last year's rank: NR

It's been an interesting year for Parnasse. In January, he defended his lightweight championship in the Polish fight promotion KSW, winning by knockout. He vacated that title to fight on the first MMA card for Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions brand. Parnasse scored a first-round knockout over Kenneth Cross on the undercard of the most-watched MMA event ever. Last month he made his UFC debut, scoring another knockout -- his sixth in a row. The first-round finish of Dan Hooker doesn't make Parnasse a contender, but he's someone to keep watching. -- Wagenheim

17. Ateba Gautier

UFC middleweight

Age: 24

Last year's rank: NR

Gautier is an absolute wrecking ball of a human. Nine of his 11 career wins have come by knockout, including seven in the first round. Potential? Off the charts. Momentum? Undeniable. The only question around Gautier isn't about him, but his opposition. His five UFC opponents have a 4-14 combined record inside the Octagon. That will change when he meets Roman Kopylov (15-5) this weekend at UFC 332. If Gautier knocks out Kopylov, his hype will be validated. -- Okamoto

18. Erin Blanchfield

UFC women's flyweight

Age: 27

2025 rank: 11

Blanchfield has been included on ESPN's list of top young prospects nearly every year since she signed with the UFC in 2021. She was ESPN's No. 1 prospect under 25 in 2023, but missed the cut the following year after suffering a one-sided drubbing to Manon Fiorot. She bounced back from that loss with back-to-back wins over Rose Namajunas and Tracy Cortez and is scheduled to take on Jasmine Jasudavicius on Oct. 17 in a battle of top-10 flyweights. -- Waters

19. Payton Talbott

UFC men's bantamweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: 20

You know a young fighter is someone the UFC considers a rising prospect when you start to see him booked against championship-decorated opponents. Talbott is coming off a December win that was convincing enough to send former two-division titlist Henry Cejudo into retirement. This weekend at UFC 332, Talbott will take on another former belt-holder, Deiveson Figueiredo. These kinds of fights draw attention, even when they're against faded stars. If Talbott is successful again, he could be on his way toward ranked opposition and a slow, steady build. -- Wagenheim

20. Lone'er Kavanagh

UFC men's flyweight

Age: 27

2025 rank: NR

He can't live on one performance forever, but Kavanagh's five-round victory over former champion Brandon Moreno in February -- in Mexico, on short notice -- said a lot about this 27-year-old's capabilities. He's 1-2 in his past three appearances, but Kavanagh has a tantalizing amount of potential. How big would a Joshua Van vs. Lone'er Kavanagh title fight be, if Kavanagh were to get on a roll and give England a shot at its next UFC champion? -- Okamoto

21. Paul Hughes

PFL lightweight

Age: 29

2025 rank: 16

Hughes came up short in two attempts to take the PFL lightweight championship from Nurmagomedov last year. Despite losing both fights by decision, Hughes proved himself to be one of the best lightweights in the world. He has been out of action this year due to a knee injury, but now that Nurmagomedov is a free agent, there's a chance for Hughes to challenge for the PFL title again immediately upon returning to active status. -- Waters

22. Gable Steveson

UFC heavyweight

Age: 26

2025 rank: NR

Steveson was about 12 seconds from being a whole lot higher on this list. As an Olympic wrestling gold medalist and two-time NCAA Division I national champion, he was as highly anticipated a prospect as the sport has seen when he transitioned to MMA last year. After winning his first four pro fights by first-round knockout, including his UFC debut in July, Steveson looked like a heavyweight with which to be reckoned. He still might turn into that guy, but getting KO'd by the second punch heavy underdog Sean Sharaf threw at him at UFC 331 two weeks ago put the brakes on the Steveson hype train. The big dude has work to do. -- Wagenheim

23. Muhammad Mokaev

Brave CF men's flyweight champion

Age: 26

2025 rank: 27

One of the most unique -- and frustrating -- careers in MMA continues to play out outside the UFC. It's now been 26 months since Mokaev parted ways with the promotion. It's worth noting that Mokaev's last fight in the UFC was a victory over Manel Kape, who is widely expected to be the next title challenger for Van. Will we ever see a day when Mokaev can return? At the moment, there doesn't seem to be much of a thaw from the UFC side. But Mokaev is still 26 years old and still unbeaten. He's so young and freakishly good that it's impossible to count out any opportunity forever. -- Okamoto

24. Valter Walker

UFC heavyweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

Walker has been the epitome of a one-trick fighter so far in his UFC career. But if his one trick isn't broken, why fix it? Since losing by unanimous decision in his UFC debut in 2024, Walker has been on an absolute tear, beating each of his past five opponents by first-round submission. Four of those finishes have come via heel hook. It wasn't until his most recent victory over Thomas Petersen that the submission ace had to show more of his ability, transitioning from his signature heel hook attempt into a calf slicer submission for the finish. -- Waters

25. David Martinez

UFC men's bantamweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

Look no further than the UFC's matchmaking to decipher how promising Martinez is. The UFC tried to pair him with Umar Nurmagomedov in July, but Martinez was forced to withdraw because of injury. He has quietly taken out some of the most respected veterans in the bantamweight division -- Dan Ige, Marlon Vera and Rob Font -- over the past 12 months and is on the cusp of a top-five ranking. Martinez lacks some of the star power of other names on this list, but he's likely to draw big-name opponents in the near future. Consistent results would inevitably skyrocket every aspect of his career. -- Okamoto

26. Tommy McMillen

UFC featherweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

McMillen, who trains with former UFC men's bantamweight champion Sean O'Malley, has had a breakout performance this year. He earned a UFC contract on "Dana White's Contender Series" a year ago and has strung together three straight wins since. He was tested in his most recent bout, a unanimous decision win over Marwan Rahiki, but he outpointed Rahiki on all three of the judges' scorecards. He's earned the right to take a step up in competition in his next Octagon appearance. -- Waters

27. Jose Miguel Delgado
UFC featherweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

Delgado was victorious in four of his first five trips to the Octagon before running into Jean Silva in the main event of Noche UFC last month. Fighting on short notice, Delgado lost by third-round submission, but he won the first round and held his own until running low on energy, whereupon Silva took over. His success in the early rounds gives Delgado building blocks for the future. -- Wagenheim

28. Raul Rosas Jr.

UFC men's bantamweight

Age: 21

2025 rank: 30

Still just 21 years old, Rosas is 7-1 in the UFC -- and the context around some of those wins is starting to grow. No longer is Rosas a phenom teenager operating on UFC prelims. Coming off his first UFC main event on Sept. 26, Rosas now holds two significant wins over proven veterans in Rob Font and Raoni Barcelos and is a ranked UFC bantamweight ... all before his 22nd birthday next week. There is no comparison to Rosas when it comes to experience gained at such a young age. There are plenty of steps between where he is now and a UFC championship, but he's certainly on the right path. -- Okamoto

29. Baisangur Susurkaev

UFC middleweight

Age: 25

2025 rank: 25

Susurkaev, a longtime training partner of former champion Khamzat Chimaev, made a name for himself last summer when he earned a UFC contract on "Dana White's Contender Series" then made his official debut four days later at UFC 319. He finished both of his opponents in those contests. In his lone appearance this year, Susurkaev picked up another finish, beating Djorden Santos by third-round submission in May. Next, he'll take on a fellow unbeaten prospect Donte Johnson at UFC 334 in November. A win over Johnson could establish Susurkaev as a future problem for top middleweight fighters. -- Waters

30. Iasmin Lucindo

UFC strawweight

Age: 24

2025 rank: 29

Lucindo had won five of six fights and was on the rise before an injury and a failed drug test in September 2025 derailed her. She withdrew from a fight with strawweight contender Gillian Robertson and ended up being suspended for a year, while Robertson went on to a title challenge. Lucindo is eligible to compete again, and at 24 years old she has time to build herself back up to contendership in the 115-pound division. -- Wagenheim

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: UEFA receives Real Madrid dossier on Barcelona-Negreira case
stories.summary: UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.
stories.body:
MADRID -- UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.

Payments made by Barcelona to companies linked to José María Enriquez Negreira -- the former vice-president of Spain's Technical Committee of Referees -- over two decades have been subject to a UEFA investigation since 2023, while there is also an ongoing Spanish criminal case.

Barcelona have said the payments, which totaled over €7 million ($7.9m), were made for technical refereeing reports.

- Ronaldo's Portugal walkout is nothing new; he has a long history of rows with coaches

- Source: Mbappé to be available for Clásico

- Raphinha back at Barça, injured in Brazil game

"UEFA can confirm that it has received from Real Madrid CF a substantial amount of documents related to the ongoing investigation into FC Barcelona in the matter involving José María Enríquez Negreira," UEFA confirmed in a statement on Thursday.

"The UEFA Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors have also received these latest documents which they will assess as part of their ongoing review."

Real Madrid said the dossier included "extensive documentation and evidence regarding events of extraordinary seriousness, which directly affect the integrity of the competition and confidence in the refereeing system."

"Real Madrid C.F. considers it essential that, now that UEFA has this documentation, the investigation proceeds with the utmost urgency until its full conclusion, and that the competent bodies take the appropriate decisions in accordance with the severity of the verified facts," the club said.

"Our club will continue to actively collaborate with UEFA and take all actions within its power to clarify events that it deems incompatible with the principles of integrity, transparency, and fair play that should govern European football."

In May, Madrid president Florentino Pérez said that the club was gathering evidence to submit a dossier to UEFA.

Having previously adopted a conciliatory tone with Barcelona -- saying in 2024 that the two clubs "have to help each other" as they worked together on the proposed European Super League -- Pérez has since been extremely critical of his LaLiga rivals.

"They've stolen seven league [titles] from me," Pérez said in May.

In a statement, Barcelona emphasized that Thursday's development did not equate to "any new proceedings."

"The proceedings were initiated in 2023, with the appointment of two investigators who have since carried out the action they deemed appropriate," Barcelona said. "The Club has always complied with all their requests. These proceedings have not been reopened because they have never been closed.

"The UEFA statement confirms receipt of documentation submitted by Real Madrid and indicates that the investigators will assess it within the framework of the existing investigation. The same text expressly refers, on two occasions, to an investigation and a review that are 'ongoing.' It therefore does not announce the opening, reopening, or reactivation of any proceedings, nor does it contain any assessment of the substance or value of the documentation provided.

"It is up to the investigators to determine what action, if any, they consider appropriate regarding this documentation. As of today, they have not made any new requests to FC Barcelona nor have they forwarded Real Madrid's complaint to the Club. Should they do so, the Club will respond accordingly, as it has done up to now.

"In accordance with the applicable legislation governing this matter, these proceedings are subject to the outcome of the criminal case currently being heard in Spain and will continue to be so."

stories.headline: Concussed Roosters star learns Grand Final fate
stories.summary: Sydney Roosters utility Connor Watson will miss the NRL grand final after failing to receive the green light to return to play inside the code's 11-day concussion stand-down period.
stories.body:
Sydney Roosters utility Connor Watson will miss the NRL Grand Final after failing to receive the green light to return to play inside the code's 11-day concussion stand-down period.

In a cruel blow, Watson will miss Sunday's decider against his former club Newcastle and become the first player to sit out a grand final as a result of a concussion.

Watson was dazed and was taken from the field moments after coming on in the Roosters' preliminary final win over the Dolphins.

Under the NRL's protocol, players diagnosed with a category-one concussion, as Watson was, face a mandatory stand-down period of 11 days.

The Roosters had indicated that Watson was testing well leading into Thursday when the 30-year-old met with an independent specialist.

But on Friday the club confirmed the utility had failed to receive clearance to line up in the grand final.

The outcome means Watson has played his last game for the Roosters with the popular utility heading to St George Illawarra next season before linking up with the PNG Chiefs in 2028.

Watson's absence likely forces Roosters coach Trent Robinson's hand when it comes to his bench, with hooker Benaiah Ioelu the most obvious man to come into Easts' 19-man squad.

Ioelu has played mostly off the bench through his 17-game NRL career and would act as cover for Reece Robson.

"I don't think it takes too much to work out what plan B is, but we have got some really good hookers," Robinson said on Thursday.

"Benaiah Ioelu played some great footy for us this year. He brings a lot of energy to us as well so he will come into consideration then."

Newcastle, meanwhile, are also expected to face a tough decision leading into Sunday's decider as they weigh up a replacement for suspended No. 9 Phoenix Crossland.

Harrison Graham has excelled as a bench option at hooker for the Knights, but coach Justin Holbrook, who doesn't have to name his final team until 90 minutes before kick-off on Sunday, has the option of also starting Thomas Cant or Diesel Hagan.

stories.headline: Dodgers commit to Skubal for Game 1 start in NLDS, source says
stories.summary: Dodgers ace Tarik Skubal will get the ball in Game 1 of the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves on Saturday, a source told ESPN on Friday.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Dodgers ace Tarik Skubal will get the ball in Game 1 of the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves on Saturday afternoon, a source told ESPN on Friday. The Dodgers are still uncertain about their plans beyond Skubal, though NL Cy Young contender Yoshinobu Yamamoto would be the logical choice.

Left-hander Skubal, acquired from the Detroit Tigers in a blockbuster trade at midseason, has won the past two American League Cy Young Awards. But there was some thought to potentially starting Yamamoto in Game 1 because it would allow both to be available for a potential winner-take-all Game 5, given that Yamamoto is accustomed to working on at least five days' rest.

The Athletic was first to report that Skubal would start Game 1.

One potential factor in the Dodgers' decision: The Braves have fared better against right-handers (.730 OPS) than lefties (.696 OPS) this season. Lining Skubal up for Games 1 and 5 probably factors into that, and it could make fellow southpaw Blake Snell a possibility for Game 2.

The Braves' plans remain in flux in the wake of their win in Game 3 of their wild-card series against Philadelphia on Thursday night. Manager Walt Weiss said from Atlanta on Friday that the team would continue to iron out its pitching plans during the flight to L.A. later that afternoon.

Weiss acknowledged he'll have to rely heavily on his bullpen in the first two games. Ace Chris Sale was previously lined up to start Sunday's Game 2, but he was used to cover four outs in the winner-take-all Game 3 against the Phillies, throwing 21 pitches.

That outing could technically count as Sale's between-starts bullpen session, coming off his Tuesday start in Game 1. But the 37-year-old left-hander has been pitching on extended rest for most of the season. Taking the ball on four days' rest, with an adrenaline-packed relief appearance in between, could be too much to take on, especially in the early round of these playoffs. Still, Weiss said him starting Game 2 remains "on the table."

"That's one of the topics of discussion this morning before we leave," Weiss said. "A lot of it's going to depend on how Chris feels. Certainly don't want to jeopardize him and his health. He just happened to feel great yesterday when he got to the park, and that's why he was in play. He's had to grind here recently. So we're going to err on the side of giving him more rest, if it's even close."

stories.summary: Carlos Baleba played his first minutes in a Manchester United shirt during a behind-closed-doors friendly on Friday.
stories.body:
Carlos Baleba played his first minutes in a Manchester United shirt during a behind-closed-doors friendly on Friday.

The 22-year-old signed from Brighton in a £70 million ($93m) deal in August but has not featured in a competitive game due to an ankle injury sustained in preseason with the Seagulls.

He did make the bench for the 1-1 draw at Fulham immediately prior to the international break and has continued working towards full fitness at the club's Carrington training complex.

Baleba took part in a training game against Swiss side Lausanne-Sport alongside fellow first-teamers including Harry Maguire and Matheus Cunha.

Head coach Michael Carrick told club media recently that Baleba was "pushing to get back as quickly as possible" from injury.

stories.headline: Williams boss vents on F1's 'cost cap trap,' leads to 'two-tier championship'
stories.summary: Formula 1's cost cap has inadvertently created a "two tier" championship, according to Williams boss James Vowles.
stories.body:
Formula 1's cost cap has inadvertently created a "two-tier" championship, according to Williams boss James Vowles.

F1 introduced the cap in 2021 in a bid to curtail spiralling costs and to level the competitive field, with several teams only narrowly scraping through the Covid-19 pandemic without going out of business.

Like other teams in the midfield, Vowles' Williams outfit have languished a long way behind the lead group of Mercedes, Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren.

Vowles said the cost cap has failed in two of the three objectives it was created to achieve and laid out why he thinks the rules need reconsidering.

"First and foremost, I own the mistakes that we made this winter, and we need to detach that from that question. We have gone backwards -- we had a car that was overweight," Vowles said in response to a question about the cost cap and how realistic it was to expect teams like Williams to cut the gap to the front.

He then gave a detailed explanation of where he thinks the mechanism has fallen short.

"But actually, when we did the cost cap, this is way back in Covid, when we had a phone call about it, there were three key tasks that we wanted out of it," he added.

"We wanted long-term financial sustainability, and I think in that goal, not just have we achieved it, but we've exceeded it. This business now has good investment that allows us to go on, and they're businesses. They weren't businesses before 2021 at all.

"The two others that went with it were sporting equity and, effectively, compression of the field, so effectively competitiveness that compressed together. Those are the three goals of cost cap, and those two have failed."

Vowles quoted data to back up his viewpoint, saying the competitiveness of F1 has worsened across the grid.

Citing statistics he had seen, Vowles said that in the cost cap era, the top four teams are scoring 83% of the points, whereas the number before the cost cap was in the 70's, and said the other teams now make the podium just 5% of the time, down from 10 before.

"In other words," he said. "We have made the situation worse ... I can give you a whole bunch of statistics, but the cost cap has made it worse, not better."

- Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Max Verstappen leads first practice from George Russell

- Why is the Bahrain Grand Prix taking place in Malaysia, 4,000 miles away? F1's unusual race explained

- Charles Leclerc tops second practice, Mercedes off the pace

Vowles has spoken often about how surprised he was when he left the all-conquering Mercedes outfit to take the top job at Williams, finding the famous old team significantly behind in resources.

He said just bringing Williams close to the level the top teams are at operationally is money that should be going into the car to bridge the performance difference.

Vowles explained what he dubbed the "cost cap trap" smaller teams have found themselves in.

"I'm probably unique because I went from the best team to the worst team. I think that's fairly clear. What I hadn't appreciated or realised when you do that jump is just how little exists.

"When you're in a cost cap, I'm not spending money on the car. I'm spending millions, tens of millions actually, just on basic systems, so you just know where a part is in the factory.

"So that's not going to the car, it's not going to a front wing, it's not going to an upgrade. It's going on systems that I need to do just to do the very basics. So, we're caught in a cost cap trap, because if I do anything short-term, and I always talk about investing in the future, now you understand why. If I do anything that's about this year, I will slow myself down in the future, and I can't do that. We have a two-tier championship. That's not me telling you that.

"That is just what is on the table right now in terms of points score. And I think, and this is where we have to come together as a business, that's not right in terms of what we want for the future. We do want the ability for, if we do a good job, we should have the ability to fight for that. Even last year, which was a great year, the gap on points between us and P4, between us and Ferrari, was 238 points. It's not a small amount. It's an absolute gulf, and we were on the podium three times.

"In cost cap, and I didn't appreciate it until I came into Williams, it really penalises you in terms of what you're doing."

Vowles said he still agrees with the concept of the cost cap but thinks it needs a radical rethink to include the gulf which historically has existed between the top and bottom teams.

"The solution isn't to take cost cap away," he added. "As I said before, we have a brilliantly financially stable sport now as a result of it, but we do need to think about what mechanisms we have in there to make sure we're all playing with the same tools and the same mechanisms, because today we're not. That's a bit lengthy, but that's my thoughts on it."

Vowles was speaking at the news conference ahead of this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Sat next to him was Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur, who offered a counter point in reply on a clear benefit of the cap.

Ferrari had famously been long-time opponents of the cost cap, but were brought around to the idea by F1 owners Liberty Media, who have guided F1 into an unprecedented commercial boom.

"What we have to keep in mind is that before the cost cap, 2018, 2017, 2016, for sure the business in general was much worse, but we had also five or six teams in bankruptcy or almost in bankruptcy," Vasseur said. "And it's not just the fact that the business is going well, it's the fact that we are sending the message that everybody can compete, right or wrong, but this is the message. And this is also attracting new investors and new OEMs (Original Equipment Manufacturer) in the business."

All of F1 teams are now considered to be valued well north of £1 billion -- for example, Forbes last year valued the Williams team at $2.5 billion for 2025.

Claire Williams, daughter of team founder Frank, had sold the team to Dorilton Capital for less than $200 million just five years earlier, in August 2020, the middle of the pandemic.

The numbers at the end of the grid are even more eye-watering.

Mercedes were valued at a record $6 billion last November after a deal which saw CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz buy a 5% stake at $300 million.

stories.headline: UFC 332 preview and picks: Why haven't there been more women's fights?
stories.summary: Top storylines and coaches' analysis for UFC 332 in Salt Lake City.
stories.body:
For all of the growth and progress of women's MMA over the past 15 years, the 2026 schedule has raised an uncomfortable -- but glaring -- question: What is happening to women's fights? Saturday's UFC 332 event in Salt Lake City will mark the first UFC event this year headlined by women, when Natalia Silva (20-5-1) and Wang Cong (10-1) meet for the vacant flyweight title. This year's lack of high-profile women's fights (and the excitement that should accompany them) has been impossible to miss. Wang, the 34-year-old Chinese challenger, has certainly felt it in the buildup to Saturday.

"Everyone was talking about how bad this main event is," Wang told ESPN, through an interpreter. "Of course I know about it. I think me and my opponent will prove them wrong, and show this is a fight they need to watch."

The sport could definitely use a boost. According to ESPN Research, the UFC has promoted 415 total bouts this year; 56 have featured women. That 13% split is the lowest mark in a decade.

The last women's fight to headline any UFC event was a non-title bout between Mackenzie Dern and Amanda Ribas in January 2025. For the last women's fight to headline a numbered event, one has to go all the way back to a bantamweight title fight between Amanda Nunes and Irene Aldana in June 2023.

Those trends are unlikely to change if some of the more underlying metrics continue to hold. Women's fights are increasingly being pushed to the prelims portion of events. In 2026, 83% of women's fights have appeared on prelims, compared with 72% in 2024, 61% in 2021 and 54% in 2017.

For their part, both Wang and Silva, a 29-year-old challenger out of Brazil, are predicting a memorable matchup Saturday. Wang is a former professional kickboxer with an aggressive style. Silva is known as more of a matador, but in 2024 when she went against Jessica Andrade, the most aggressive opponent of her UFC career, they won fight of the night.

"For sure, it's going to be a well-fought battle," Silva told ESPN through an interpreter. "She comes in aggressive, which gives me the opportunity to be aggressive as well. What I can tell people is that's going to be an incredible fight."

One thing is undeniable, Wang and Silva have a rare opportunity on Saturday to headline a numbered event with a women's title fight.

More storylines to watch
Gautier is getting the step up in competition he asked for
Ateba Gautier is an athletic, 24-year-old wrecking ball from Cameroon with a 5-0 record in the UFC that includes four knockouts. The combined record of his opponents, however, has been 4-14. That doesn't diminish what Gautier has done, but it's still unknown how he will fare against tougher competition.

For his part, Gautier isn't shying away from challenging himself. Immediately following his last win in May, Gautier called for a fight with former middleweight champion Israel Adesanya -- arguably the greatest 185-pound fighter of all time. The UFC didn't give him Adesanya, but he did get Roman Kopylov, a 35-year-old Russian with 12 UFC bouts. A win wouldn't validate Gautier as a title contender, but it would prove he's ready for greater tests.

Wint could be the sleeper breakout candidate of the card
In terms of fighters who can make an individual splash at UFC 332, Wang and Silva in the main event stand out. Payton Talbott taking on a former champion in Deiveson Figueiredo is an obvious one. Undefeated Jacobe Smith is a finishing machine, and the aforementioned Gautier is in the biggest fight of his career.

Quietly, Anthony Wint could steal the show. Wint's prelim fight against Lucas Armand will be his third in less than two months. He's a former collegiate and NFL linebacker, fighting out of a notoriously talented and striking-oriented gym in Kill Cliff FC. He already is very much on UFC CEO Dana White's radar, having earned his contract on "Contender Series" on Aug. 11. If he does something spectacular, expect White to give it attention in his postfight comments (which in turn, draws everyone's attention).

Coaches' questions for women's flyweight championship
'What is Natalia Silva's game plan under pressure?'

Cong's striking is on point. She is aggressive with it, but she makes mistakes with it as well. I feel like Silva is the more well-rounded fighter, and it's up to her to take advantage of that. If this fight does go to the ground, I think Silva will present bigger problems -- and I see that as a path to victory for her. Wang is going to look for the knockout, and because of that, she will overextend in certain positions. I have a gut feeling Silva is going to work some ground work into this one. Silva is so good at controlling the pace of a fight, but with Cong coming at her so aggressively, I think she'll be forced to try different stuff. It's a pick 'em fight. -- John Wood, Syndicate MMA

Who will own the 'second exchange'?
Silva's path to victory is about space, timing and making Wang reset. Silva needs to use her movement and feints to keep Wang from getting comfortable and building combinations. Silva is best at range, not standing in the pocket. Her counters matter in this matchup. She doesn't just survive Wang's pressure, she scores with midrange kicks and southpaw counters after Wang overcommits. For Wang, it's about pressure without chasing. She needs to cut the cage. Containing Silva becomes the real job. This is where her low kick and body work become weapons. Silva's movement is a huge part of her defense. If Wang can consistently attack the legs and body, she can start shrinking the cage without simply chasing. Who controls what happens after the initial exchange? If Wang attacks, Silva counters and exits, that's Silva's fight. If Wang attacks, Silva tries to exit and Wang cuts her off, those are the moments Wang wants. Whoever imposes their will on that second exchange wins. -- Eric Nicksick, Xtreme Couture

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: Capitals face Hurricanes in a critical early-season clash
stories.summary: Both are expected to challenge for the Metro Division title. Plus, what to watch in the other four games, updated stat leaders and more.
stories.body:
The 2026-27 NHL season is not yet a week old, but it's been a bit of a roller-coaster ride:

Nathan MacKinnon fought Brandt Clarke, then fired his helmet at the boards in celebration.
Evan Bouchard had three goals and two assists on opening night ... and somehow that wasn't enough to beat the Canucks. Connor McDavid equaled his five points on Thursday, and the Oilers won 9-7.
Igor Shesterkin scored the first goalie goal in Rangers history.
And commissioner Gary Bettman cautioned about the further use of no-trade clauses after they became the story in hockey this summer.

So much for easing into the campaign!

There's no slowing down Friday, as the five-game slate includes some more season debuts. That includes Alex Ovechkin and the Washington Capitals, who take on the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes. Both teams are expected to contend for the Metro Division crown, and every result counts.

Here's what else to watch in each game this evening:

New York Rangers at Detroit Red Wings

6:30 p.m. ET (TNT) | DET -142, O/U: 5.5

The Rangers' season didn't get off to the best start, as they couldn't get a puck past Jeremy Swayman while the Bruins put two past Igor Shesterkin and one into an empty net. It could be worse, though; just ask a Red Wings fan.

Detroit's captain, Dylan Larkin, asked for a trade, then was stripped of his captaincy upon his return to camp following the lack of a deal and is now out with an upper-body injury; rising star defenseman (and restricted free agent) Simon Edvinsson is without a contract; and the club has not named a permanent GM to handle these matters. Of course, the Wings do have some exciting players that will be taking the ice, including Moritz Seider, Lucas Raymond and Alex DeBrincat. Let's see how they can tune out the off-ice issues.

Washington Capitals at Carolina Hurricanes

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | CAR -148, O/U: 6.5

Despite an overtime loss to the Panthers on Tuesday, the Hurricanes look just as strong as the group that won the Cup last season; that makes sense, since the majority of the roster is back and ready for another run. Meanwhile, the Capitals spent the summer making bold move after bold move -- and welcomed Ovechkin officially back for one more season as well. This early clash could set the tone for the battles to come. (Round 2 will be Oct. 13, again in Raleigh.)

Boston Bruins at Winnipeg Jets

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | WPG -122, O/U: 5.5

This will be the season debut for the Jets, and they'll be playing without Connor Hellebuyck, the 2025 winner of both the Hart Trophy as league MVP and the Vezina Trophy as the NHL's top goaltender. Hellebuyck's trade request has thus far gone unaccommodated, leaving Stuart Skinner in the Winnipeg crease.

On the other side, the B's got off to a steady start with a 3-0 win over the Rangers on opening night and hope to carry some momentum into this cross-conference tilt before a matchup against the Wild on Saturday.

St. Louis Blues at Dallas Stars

9 p.m. ET (TNT) | DAL -205, O/U: 5.5

This game will be the season debut for both clubs and the first regular-season game with Robert Thomas serving as Blues captain. The Blues have become a popular hipster pick to earn a wild-card playoff spot this season, while you'd be hard-pressed to find anyone not predicting the Stars will finish among the top three in the Western Conference -- particularly now that Jason Robertson is officially back (at least for this season).

Anaheim Ducks at Vegas Golden Knights

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | VGK -185, O/U: 6.5

The last time these two teams met was May 14, when the Golden Knights closed out their second-round playoff series with a 5-1 win. In the time since, Vegas lost in the Stanley Cup Final, elected not to continue John Tortorella's tenure as head coach (opting for Ryan Craig) and traded its top goal scorer from last season, Pavel Dorofeyev, to the Rangers.

The Ducks lost their three veteran blueliners from last year's squad (John Carlson, Jacob Trouba and Radko Gudas), weathered the Leo Carlsson offer sheet storm, then signed long-term new deals with Cutter Gauthier and Tristan Luneau. How will the two Pacific Division rivals look Friday?

stories.headline: St. Louis up to 2nd place with unbeaten run now at 17 games
stories.summary: Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.

St. Louis (13-6-8) extended its unbeaten streak to 17 matches in MLS play and moved up to second place in MLS' Western Conference table.

New York (9-12-6) entered having conceded just two goals in its last four games, with Ethan Horvath recording three shutouts.

The Red Bulls had won their last two games, but were without rising stars Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall for the game, with the pair away on national team duty for the United States.

Rafael Navarro opened the scoring just five minutes into the game when he redirected Conrad Wallem's header across the goal.

Becher capitalized on a New York turnover deep in its own half to make it 2-0 in the 87th minute. Ostrak sent in a rebound in stoppage time.

Roman Bürki made four saves to earn his third clean sheet of the season for St. Louis.

It was the first time New York and St. Louis have met during the regular season.

St. Louis hosts the LA Galaxy next on Oct. 11, while the Red Bulls play San Diego FC at home the day before.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Toby Greene joins Geelong on day one of AFL free agency
stories.summary: The AFL has revealed Greater Western Sydney's compensation draft pick after former skipper Toby Greene completed his late-career move to Geelong.
stories.body:
Toby Greene has become the first major AFL free agency domino to fall, with Greater Western Sydney to receive a second-round draft pick for losing their former captain to Geelong.

The Cats lodged paperwork on Friday to land the inaugural Giant as an unrestricted free agent.

Greene, a triple All Australian and dual club champion, booted 450 goals across his 15-year, 282-game tenure for GWS.

The 33-year-old cited family reasons for returning to his native Victoria and reunites with his close mate and former Giants forward Jeremy Cameron at the Cattery on a lucrative three-year deal.

The Giants will receive a second round draft selection as compensation, currently slated at No.26.

Earlier, key forward Joel Amartey's switch from Sydney to Carlton was confirmed as the free agency period opened.

The Swans will receive draft compensation for losing the unrestricted 27-year-old, who was an emergency during finals after failing to convince coach Dean Cox following a partial Achilles tear.

Paperwork will be lodged later on Friday to rubber stamp Lachie Neale's move to Collingwood as an unrestricted free agent after the Brisbane Lions star added a third premiership medal to his swag of silverware.

Melbourne's 2021 premiership vice-captain Jack Viney is poised for a move with two years remaining on his contract after meeting with West Coast.

After being sidelined through injury for all but one game this season, the 32-year-old was told by coach Steven King there would likely be limited opportunities for him in the Demons midfield.

"Footy's gone that way mate," Viney told 10 News at Perth Airport on Thursday.

"So took a bit to process early days, but we're here now, so we'll make the best of the opportunity ... it (a deal) will get done."

Young Hawthorn forward Calsher Dear, meanwhile, has opted to stay at the Hawks on a two-year deal after weighing up a potential move to the Dees.

The 21-year-old, son of late 1991 Norm Smith medallist Paul Dear, burst onto the scene in his debut season with 25 goals from 17 appearances in 2024.

But the emerging tall has struggled to hold his spot through injury and internal competition, adding just 14 games in 2025 and 2026.

"We are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond," Hawks list manager Mark McKenzie said.

Hawthorn's key forward selection squeeze is set to worsen in 2027, with Gold Coast's restricted free agent Ben King expected to join Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis, Mabior Chol and Dear.

stories.headline: Bruise Crew: Knights duo settle on nickname
stories.summary: Newcastle's rising back-rowers Francis Manuleleua and Jermaine McEwen want their own identity and have shunned the 'Bash Brothers' moniker.
stories.body:
The emergence of the raw-boned back-row duo of Jermaine McEwen and Francis Manuleleua has been critical to Newcastle's run to the NRL grand final.

But as commentators look for a nickname that best sums up the Knights' gruesome twosome, the pair are clear that they don't want to be known as a cheap imitation of what's gone before.

"We don't want to be called the Bash Brothers, because that's already taken, we've got to figure something out," said McEwen.

'The Bash Brothers' was a moniker given to Penrith duo Moses Leota and James Fisher-Harris during the Panthers' run to four-straight premierships.

Penrith edge forwards Joe Galuvao and Tony Puletua were christened 'the Hair Bears' in 2003, while Canberra's devastating centre-wing combination of Joey Leilua and Jordan Rapana was dubbed 'Leipana' a decade ago.

So when a list of potential nicknames is put to McEwen and Manuleleua ahead of Sunday's clash against the Sydney Roosters, the duo settle on one name for their hard-hitting partnership.

"The Bruise Crew, I like that one," Manuleleua said.

It's a fitting tag for the pair, who have come from relative obscurity to feature in this year's decider all while trampling or folding anybody who stands in their way.

The 21-year-old McEwen, was running around in the Koori Knockout on grand final weekend last year.

McEwen, who only has 39 first grade games to his name, showed he won't be intimidated when he barked at Leota in the Knights' energy-sapping win over Penrith.

"You probably don't want to hang around us too much because we just muck around too much," Manuleleua said.

"But when it comes to training and game day, we flick that switch and we're just ready to bang."

Manuleleua is just 14 games into his NRL career and not so long ago the 22-year-old was mowing the grass outside Penrith's centre of excellence.

In last week's preliminary final win over the Panthers he scored the opening try and pulled off a terrific try-saver to stop Brian To'o.

McEwen hopes he and Manuleleua, who room together, will line up alongside each other for Samoa at the World Cup.

"We both lean on each other a lot with each other's energy," McEwen said.

"I was always burning energy thinking about the game and he's just a chill guy, but on gameday he's a beast, bro.

"We just love playing with each other because you bring that energy and want to go out there and bang."
